title: Which numbers are both a square and a cube?
description: Sixty four is both a square and a cube, so six equal factors are grouped in twos and in threes. The same grouping is tried on three and on four, and then on any number, and every result is checked by multiplying.
teaching_notes: One idea: six equal factors can be grouped as two groups of three or as three groups of two, so the number is both a square and a cube. Watch for students who think any square number is also a cube number.

video_script.why: The child can write four to the power six as a power of a power in two ways and now uses that to find every number that is both a square and a cube.
video_script.substitution: Sixty four, then seven hundred twenty nine and four thousand ninety six, each split into groups of equal factors two ways.
video_script.anchor: six equal factors in a row on the board, grouped in twos and then in threes
video_script.payoff_line: Such numbers are the sixth powers

final_answer.value: Yes, infinitely many: the sixth powers, such as 1, 64, 729 and 4096
final_answer.spoken: yes, infinitely many: the sixth powers, such as one, sixty four, seven hundred twenty nine and four thousand ninety six

never_show: the name sixth power before the answer beat
maths_rules: n × n × n × n × n × n = (n³)² = (n²)³, so every sixth power is a square and a cube
video_script.design: One idea: six equal factors group in twos and in threes. The row of six factors stays on the board all video; the name of such numbers is held until the answer; the check multiplies the groups back.

beats.on_screen: title card, From your book; 64 = 8² and 64 = 4³ on the board

marks.book: the title card From your book arrives
marks.ask: a question mark appears beside them

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about square and cube numbers.
<bookmark mark='sixtyfour'/>Sixty four is a square number, eight squared, and a cube number, four cubed.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Are there other numbers that are both squares and cubes?
And can we describe all such numbers in general?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: square number: 2 equal factors; cube number: 3 equal factors

marks.square: two equal factors are drawn in a row
marks.cube: three equal factors are drawn in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='square'/>A square number is two equal factors multiplied.
<bookmark mark='cube'/>A cube number is three equal factors multiplied.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, sixty four is eight squared, and also four cubed.

beats.on_screen: To find: other numbers that are both squares and cubes; a way to describe them in general
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find other numbers that are both squares and cubes.
<bookmark mark='describe'/>Then we describe all such numbers in general.

beats.on_screen: 64 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2; two groups of three: (2³)² = 8²; three groups of two: (2²)³ = 4³

marks.one: 64 is written as six 2s in a row
marks.split: the six 2s are split into groups
marks.twothree: two groups of three 2s are boxed, giving 8²
marks.threetwo: three groups of two 2s are boxed, giving 4³

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, sixty four is six twos multiplied.
<bookmark mark='split'/>Split them into groups, the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='twothree'/>Two groups of three twos make eight squared.
<bookmark mark='threetwo'/>Three groups of two twos make four cubed.

marks.two: six 3s are written in a row
marks.grouped: 27² and 9³ are written under the two groupings

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, try six threes multiplied.
<bookmark mark='grouped'/>Two groups of three threes make twenty seven squared.
Three groups of two threes make nine cubed.

marks.three: six 4s are written in a row
marks.grouped: 64² and 16³ are written under the two groupings

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, try six fours multiplied.
<bookmark mark='grouped'/>Two groups of three fours make sixty four squared.
Three groups of two fours make sixteen cubed.

beats.on_screen: n × n × n × n × n × n = (n³)² and (n²)³

marks.four: any number is written six times in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step four, take any number multiplied six times.
<bookmark mark='general'/>It groups as the cube of the number, all squared.
<bookmark mark='also'/>It also groups as the square of the number, all cubed.
Either way, it is both a square and a cube.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check by multiplying.
Twenty seven times twenty seven is seven hundred twenty nine.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>Nine times nine times nine is also seven hundred twenty nine.
<bookmark mark='big'/>Sixty four times sixty four is four thousand ninety six.
<bookmark mark='sixteen'/>Sixteen times sixteen times sixteen is also four thousand ninety six.
<bookmark mark='one'/>One is one squared and one cubed.

beats.on_screen: Answer: yes, infinitely many; the sixth powers, such as 1, 64, 729 and 4096

marks.a2: the sixth powers is written and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='a1'/>Yes, there are infinitely many such numbers.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>Such numbers are the sixth powers.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>Examples are one, sixty four, seven hundred twenty nine and four thousand ninety six.
